initial_scene: A dark blue, white-faced clock stands upright on the central pink plate. The light green target plate is on the robot right; the blue plate on the left is empty. Both robot forearms enter from the near camera side. A person across the table holds a keyboard but does not interact with the clock or hands.

observed_sequence.action: The right arm moves its open hand inward from above the green plate toward the clock on the pink plate. The left hand remains raised and open above the left side of the table.
The right hand surrounds the clock casing, lowering its fingers to opposite sides as the clock remains on the pink plate.
The right fingers close around the casing and begin lifting; the clock becomes firmly held and rises away from its initial support.
The right arm lifts the clock clear of the pink plate and carries it rightward over the green plate, adjusting the held clock toward upright. The left hand supplies no support.
The right arm lowers the upright clock into the green plate area. Its lower base and the exact support contact are partly hidden by the hand.

The clock remains upright in the green plate area. The right fingers begin opening at the ending while the hand stays close around its lower sides; no subsequent withdrawal or independently unsupported state is shown.

arm_hand_roles.left: Open and raised over the left table area, with slight incidental motion; does not touch the clock or support the manipulation.

This egocentric paired-arm arrangement supports robot-relative right, consistent with the original instruction.
